title: Local institutions in Peru and the presence and number of fast-food outlets
abstract: This paper studies whether local institutional quality helps explain where fast-food outlets enter and how many operate in urban districts of Peru, where many districts have no outlets. The authors develop a market-entry framework in which demand, infrastructure, and local government institutions shape the equilibrium number of businesses. They build institutional-quality measures from municipal administrative and organizational characteristics and estimate separate relationships for outlet presence and outlet counts using a zero-inflated Poisson model. Institutional quality is most clearly associated with whether an outlet is present; urban-development management, information systems, and municipal investment-planning offices are among the relevant factors. The findings link effective local institutions with infrastructure that can lower business-entry costs, while data limitations prevent the study from assessing several other potential entry conditions.
